outcome: Vaginal birth after cesarean (VBAC) success rate
Composite maternal outcome (uterine rupture/dehiscence, postpartum hemorrhage, intrapartum/postpartum fever)
cohort: 1,397 women with one prior cesarean delivery and no prior vaginal births undergoing labor after cesarean (LAC) between March 2011 and March 2020
finding: VBAC rates decreased as the duration of the second stage of labor increased, but remained relatively high even with prolonged second stage.
mod_finding: Operative vaginal and cesarean deliveries were significantly more likely as second stage duration time interval increased.
